display.title: Episode 372: The Blessing of a Tzaddik, Chapter 2 (Shabbos HaGadol)
display.summary_short: Before Pesach: why Shabbos HaGadol is great, how children can help get ready, and how a blessing from the Baal Shem Tov kept an innkeeper young.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Shabbos HaGadol, a few days before Pesach 5749. Uncle Yossi explains what makes this Shabbos great: we read part of the Haggadah, from Avadim Hayinu through Dayenu, and on the tenth of Nissan the Egyptian firstborn rose against their own people, as Dovid HaMelech writes in Tehillim. Then a to-do list for Hashem's soldiers before Pesach: honor your parents by helping clean and change over the dishes, arrange the sale of chametz through a rav, and invite anyone without a Seder to join yours. After a Pesach-themed Hakochainik march, a second-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school leads the Shema and introduces themselves. Story time concludes The Blessing of a Tzaddik: the young-looking innkeeper tells Reb Boruch that sixty years ago the Baal Shem Tov stayed at his inn. Sweeping the room at night, he noticed the tzaddik's shoes set in a strange position and left them untouched; the Baal Shem Tov thanked him and blessed him with long life. Ever since, he has looked thirty though he is ninety, while the old-looking man is his own son. In the mailbox, a girl tells how she brought a lonely girl into the dancing at a simchah. The show ends with the newsletter's 'Cleanup' mitzvah card and candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Respect a tzaddik and everything that belongs to him, and prepare yourself with mitzvos, so that a tzaddik's blessing can reach you in full.
